traceability.evidence:
Story and traceability: - Story file exists: docs/stories/009.0-DEV-MAINTENANCE-TOOLS.story.md - All maintenance-related modules and tests reference this story via @story and @req tags (e.g., src/maintenance/index.ts, cli.ts, detect.ts, update.ts, batch.ts, report.ts, utils.ts, commands.ts; tests/maintenance/*.test.ts).
Core maintenance functionality (REQ-MAINT-DETECT, REQ-MAINT-UPDATE, REQ-MAINT-BATCH, REQ-MAINT-VERIFY, REQ-MAINT-REPORT, REQ-MAINT-SAFE): - Detection of stale annotations (REQ-MAINT-DETECT): - src/maintenance/detect.ts: - export function detectStaleAnnotations(codebasePath: string): string[] - Resolves a workspaceRoot from cwd + codebasePath; returns [] early if root is missing or not a directory. - Uses getAllFiles(workspaceRoot) from src/maintenance/utils.ts to recursively gather files. - Scans file content with /@story\s+([^\s]+)/g, handles each match with handleStoryMatch. - Uses isUnsafeStoryPath and enforceProjectBoundary (from src/utils/storyReferenceUtils) to skip unsafe paths and enforce that only in-project candidates are checked. - Calls fs.existsSync only on in-project candidates and collects story paths as stale when no in-project candidate exists on disk. - src/maintenance/utils.ts: - getAllFiles(dir: string): string[] safely returns [] if dir doesn’t exist or isn’t a directory and otherwise recursively traverses directories, collecting files. - Tests: - tests/maintenance/detect.test.ts: - "[REQ-MAINT-DETECT] should return empty array when no stale annotations". - "[REQ-MAINT-DETECT] should detect stale annotation references" (creates a file with @story stale.story.md and verifies result contains that name). - tests/maintenance/detect-isolated.test.ts: - Returns [] for non-existent directory. - Detects stale annotations in nested directories. - Checks behavior on permission-denied directory (throws in the low-level function). - Verifies security behavior: unsafe relative/absolute/invalid-extension story paths are not passed to fs.existsSync, while normalized in-workspace paths are checked.
- Updating annotation references (REQ-MAINT-UPDATE): - src/maintenance/update.ts: - export function updateAnnotationReferences(codebasePath, oldPath, newPath): number. - Validates codebasePath exists and is a directory; returns 0 otherwise. - Escapes oldPath into a safe regex and builds /(@story\s*)/g. - getAllFiles(codebasePath) provides file list, processFileForAnnotationUpdates performs replacements with a callback that only changes @story occurrences, increments a count, and writes back only when content changes. - Tests: - tests/maintenance/update-isolated.test.ts: - "[REQ-MAINT-UPDATE] updates @story annotations in files" — verifies count === 1 and file now contains "@story new.path.md". - Returns 0 when directory does not exist. - tests/maintenance/update.test.ts: - Returns 0 when no updates are made for given root/paths.
- Batch operations and verification (REQ-MAINT-BATCH, REQ-MAINT-VERIFY): - src/maintenance/batch.ts: - batchUpdateAnnotations(codebasePath, mappings) loops over mappings and sums updateAnnotationReferences results (pure batch helper). - verifyAnnotations(codebasePath): boolean uses detectStaleAnnotations and returns stale.length === 0. - Tests (tests/maintenance/batch.test.ts): - batchUpdateAnnotations returns 0 for empty mappings. - verifyAnnotations returns true when @story points to an existing .story.md file.
- Reporting and safety (REQ-MAINT-REPORT, REQ-MAINT-SAFE): - src/maintenance/report.ts: - generateMaintenanceReport(codebasePath): string calls detectStaleAnnotations; returns "" when none, otherwise a newline-separated list of stale story paths. - Tests (tests/maintenance/report.test.ts): - Returns empty string when no stale annotations. - Returns a string containing the stale story path when present.
CLI and integration (Core Functionality, Integration, User Experience, Error Handling): - CLI wiring and commands: - package.json defines a binary: - "bin": { "traceability-maint": "lib/src/maintenance/cli.js" } (integration into the published package). - src/maintenance/flags.ts: - parseCliInput/normalizeCliArgs separate node, script, subcommand, args. - parseFlags supports --root, --json, --format (throws on invalid values), --from, --to, --dry-run; default root is process.cwd(). - src/maintenance/commands.ts: - Defines exit codes: EXIT_OK=0, EXIT_STALE=1, EXIT_USAGE=2. - handleDetect: uses parseFlags + detectStaleAnnotations, prints text or JSON {root, stale}, returns 0 or 1 depending on results. - handleVerify: uses verifyAnnotations; prints success or guidance and returns 0 or 1. - handleReport: uses generateMaintenanceReport and respects --format text/json; prints Markdown-style or JSON report and always returns 0. - handleUpdate: validates --from/--to, supports --dry-run (no changes, uses generateMaintenanceReport as an estimate, outputs human/JSON summary), or performs real update via updateAnnotationReferences and prints summary; returns 0 on success or 2 for usage errors. - src/maintenance/cli.ts: - runMaintenanceCli(rawArgv): normalizes arguments, dispatches to appropriate handler based on subcommand. - Handles help / no subcommand by printing help and returning EXIT_OK. - Catches unexpected errors, prints "traceability-maint failed: " and returns EXIT_USAGE. - printHelp describes commands detect/verify/report/update and all supported options (--root, --json, --format, --from, --to, --dry-run, -h/--help).
- CLI tests (tests/maintenance/cli.test.ts) cover user experience and error handling for the story’s requirements: - detect with empty temp dir: exit 0 with "No stale @story annotations found.". - verify with matching story file: exit 0 and a single log line. - report: prints a human-readable Markdown-style report including the stale story name, exit 0. - update: performs replacement and exits 0, updated file contains new @story path. - update missing --from/--to: exits 2, logs an error and prints help (logs confirmed via spies). - dry-run: exits 0, does not modify files (content equality assertion), logs summary. - report with invalid --format: exits 2 with error containing "Invalid format: yaml" and guidance that only text/json are allowed. - detect with --json and stale annotation: exits 1, prints JSON with array payload.stale including stale.story.md. - detect with non-existent --root: exits 0 with "No stale @story annotations found.". - No subcommand: prints usage/help banner, exits 0, no error logged. - Simulated filesystem permission error on detect: exits 2 and logs an error prefixed with "traceability-maint failed:".
Integration into plugin, documentation, and exports: - src/maintenance/index.ts exports maintenance tools and tags the story and REQ IDs. - src/index.ts imports the five maintenance functions and exports them under a maintenance object alongside rules and configs, with @story 009.0 and @req REQ-MAINTENANCE-API-EXPORT. - README.md, “Maintenance CLI” section: - Describes traceability-maint purpose and commands (detect, verify, report, update). - Provides concrete usage examples for each, including an update example that matches the implementation. - user-docs/api-reference.md, “Maintenance API and CLI” section: - Documents signatures, behavior, and return values for detectStaleAnnotations, updateAnnotationReferences, batchUpdateAnnotations, verifyAnnotations, and generateMaintenanceReport. - Documents traceability-maint CLI: global options, command behavior, exit codes, and JSON/text outputs, consistent with implementation.
Test execution evidence: - package.json defines "test": "jest --ci --bail". - Invocations via tooling show Jest being run; no specific test failures or stack traces were reported for these commands, and the maintenance-specific tests are present, focused, and aligned with the story’s requirements.
Overall, the code, tests, and documentation together demonstrate that the maintenance tools detect stale annotations, perform updates and batch operations, verify post-state, produce reports, expose a CLI integrated with the project, and handle errors and safety concerns as specified.
traceability.notes: The 009.0-DEV-MAINTENANCE-TOOLS story is fully implemented. Dedicated maintenance modules implement detection of stale @story references, targeted in-place updates, batch updates, verification, and reporting. These are exposed both as a programmatic API through the plugin’s maintenance export and as a CLI (traceability-maint) with subcommands, flags, clear exit codes, and dry-run support. Tests under tests/maintenance comprehensively exercise each function and CLI command, including success paths, edge cases, and error conditions, and they are explicitly tagged to this story and its requirements. User-facing documentation in README.md and user-docs/api-reference.md describes the maintenance behavior and CLI usage consistently with the code. All acceptance criteria—core functionality, quality preservation, integration with the existing structure, user feedback, error handling, and documentation—are satisfied, so the assessment status is PASSED.
